proposal: The Mandate says enhanced statutory authority for local autonomy should extend to prioritizing rental subsidies that emphasize choice and mobility in vouchers over site-based subsidies, and to giving public housing agencies maximal flexibility to direct land sales involving existing public housing so land can be put to greater economic use. It asks Congress to consider the future of the public housing model, doubting that new investment beyond maintenance serves upward mobility, while cautioning that the turn to mobility vouchers must not come at the expense of local autonomy.

status_summary: No statute or executive action was found that gives public housing agencies broad authority to direct sales of public housing land or that prioritizes mobility-oriented vouchers over site-based subsidies, so the steps found are parallel to the recommendation. On 2026-07-11 Public Law 119-101 removed the end date of the Rental Assistance Demonstration and raised its public housing conversion cap from 455,000 to 555,000 units (section 212), moving more public housing to other rental assistance platforms; its table of contents lists no section on public housing disposition, land sales or voucher mobility, and a CRS summary describes none. HUD Notice PIH 2026-23, issued 2026-08-28 under existing Section 18 authority, eased demolition and disposition rules, including a very-small-PHA threshold of 75 or fewer units and functional obsolescence as a basis, while requiring fair market value for sales unless HUD approves a below-market transaction, and it sets terms for ground leases and disposal of excess vacant land. The FY2027 budget request of 2026-04-03 would bar most new vouchers for new families, which runs against the mobility emphasis.

timeline.event: HUD's FY2027 budget request proposed barring most new vouchers for new families.
